flags.why: Calling someone a pig because of their weight can be insulting, even when intended as teasing.
flags.fix: Add derogatory to the existing tags.

flags.why: The example explains the unit instead of showing it in use.
flags.fix: Tôi mua ba mã vải để may rèm. = I bought three yards of fabric to make curtains.

flags.why: This sense denotes the crossbar of a harrow, not a rake ([dictionary](https://vi.wiktionary.org/wiki/m%C3%A3)).
flags.fix: crossbar of a harrow (holding the teeth); example: Mã bừa bị gãy nên phải thay. = The harrow's crossbar broke and needs replacing.

flags.why: This sense means a batch weighed in one weighing, rather than any object placed on a scale ([dictionary](https://v2.rung.vn/dict/vn_vn/M%C3%A3)).
flags.fix: batch weighed in a single weighing; example: Phải cân hai mã mới hết số thóc này. = It takes two weighings to weigh all this paddy.

flags.why: Using cắn for hostile verbal attacks online is current colloquial usage, not dated.
The first example explains the traditional classification instead of showing the term in ordinary use.
flags.fix: Remove the first example and retain: Uống rượu nhiều hại cả lục phủ ngũ tạng. = Heavy drinking harms all your internal organs.

flags.why: This spelling preserves the insulting force of cút when used to tell someone to get lost.
flags.fix: Add offensive to the existing tags.

flags.why: Learners frequently encounter rang meaning to fry rice, which the roasting gloss does not cover ([usage](https://congan.baclieu.gov.vn/ch10/465-Kinh-nghiem-lam-mon-com-rang-ngon.mhtml)).
flags.fix: to fry (rice, stirring it in a pan); example: Tôi đang rang cơm với trứng. = I'm frying rice with eggs.

flags.why: The entry omits the everyday use after adjectives to express or urge an increase in degree.
flags.fix: more; indicates an increase in the preceding quality, often in requests; example: Nói to lên một chút nhé. = Speak a little louder, please.

flags.why: The explicitly contemptuous use for people lacks a derogatory warning tag.
flags.fix: Add derogatory for the contemptuous use referring to people; the animal use is neutral.
